findings.title: TotalDocs reads bleveBackend.cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: `TotalDocs()` iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. Although `searchSupport.init` calls `s.search.TotalDocs()` after `group.Wait()`, the watch goroutine started a few lines earlier on lines 207-213 of `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go` is already running and can concurrently invoke `handleEvent` -> `getOrCreateIndex` -> `BuildIndex`, which mutates `b.cache[key] = idx` under `b.cacheMu.Lock()`. In addition, any other caller of `TotalDocs` after startup will race with on-demand index creation in `Search` or `handleEvent`. In Go, concurrent map iteration and map write causes a fatal runtime panic (`concurrent map iteration and map write`). `TotalDocs` should acquire `b.cacheMu.RLock()` / `defer b.cacheMu.RUnlock()`.

findings.title: Removing the mutex from BuildIndex allows concurrent builds of the same NamespacedResource
findings.body: Previously `BuildIndex` held `b.cacheMu.Lock()` for its entire execution, which serialized index builds. With the lock moved to only wrap `b.cache[key] = idx` at line 137, two concurrent callers of `getOrCreateIndex` for the same `NamespacedResource` (for example, concurrent `Search` requests for an unindexed namespace or a `Search` racing with `handleEvent`) will both see `GetIndex == nil` and run `BuildIndex` in parallel. For file-backed indexes (`size > b.opts.FileThreshold`), the second `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` on the same directory will fail because the directory already exists / BoltDB file lock is held, failing the request; for in-memory indexes, both will build an index and one will overwrite the other in `b.cache`, while `IndexMetrics.IndexTenants` and `IndexMetrics.IndexedKinds` are incremented twice for the same key. Per-key synchronization (e.g., `singleflight` or a per-key lock) is needed when building an index.

findings.title: Data race on totalBatchesIndexed and shared err in searchSupport.init errgroup
findings.body: When `s.initWorkers > 1` (the PR description specifically notes high concurrency when building namespaces), the `group.Go` goroutines in `searchSupport.init` concurrently execute `totalBatchesIndexed++` (line 189) and assign to the outer `err` variable in `_, _, err = s.build(...)` (line 190) without synchronization. Because `BuildIndex` no longer serializes these goroutines with a global mutex, these unsynchronized writes now execute in parallel, causing a data race under `-race` and potentially corrupting the error returned by the goroutine or the `totalBatchesIndexed` count. Use a local `_, _, err := s.build(...)` inside the closure and either `atomic.Int64` for `totalBatchesIndexed` or `len(stats)`.

findings.title: NewResourceServer leaks background context and blob bucket when s.Init fails
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` creates a cancellable context `ctx, cancel` (line 229) and optionally opens a blob bucket (line 208) before calling `s.Init(ctx)` at line 258. If `s.Init(ctx)` returns an error, `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()` (and if `s.search.init` succeeded before `s.initWatcher` failed, the watch goroutine in `searchSupport.init` is also left running). `cancel()` should be called on the error path before returning.
